blocks.text: The IUPAC rules for naming alkenes resemble those for alkanes.

items: Select the longest continuous chain that contains the C=C as the parent chain, and change the ending of the alkane name of the same length from -ane to -ene.
Number the chain so as to include both carbon atoms of the double bond, beginning from the end nearer the double bond.
Designate the location of the double bond by the number of the first atom of the double bond as a prefix.
Indicate the locations of substituent groups by the numbers of the carbon atoms to which they are attached.
If the parent chain contains more than one double bond, the compounds are alkadienes for two, alkatrienes for three, and so on.

blocks.prompt: Name CH3C(CH3)=CH-CH3 and CH2=CHCH(CH3)2, and draw 3-methylbut-2-ene (Quick Check 11.4b, c).
blocks.explanation: CH3C(CH3)=CHCH3: a four-carbon chain with the double bond at C2 and a methyl on C2, 2-methylbut-2-ene. CH2=CHCH(CH3)2: a four-carbon chain with the double bond at C1 and a methyl on C3, 3-methylbut-1-ene. 3-Methylbut-2-ene (printed 3-methyl-2-butene) is CH3CH=C(CH3)CH3, which by the lowest-number rule is the same molecule as 2-methylbut-2-ene.

items: Longest chain containing C=C, -ane to -ene; number from the end nearer the double bond; the double bond's first carbon gives the locant; substituents numbered; two double bonds: -diene, three: -triene.
